resources.string: Off by default. Safe mode skips all operations.
Only supported live operations. Dynamic kstat requires the next normal boot.
Root temporarily unavailable · retry after authorization
Wait for the path to appear
Enable boot application and make SUSFS available before mounting. Snapshot before mounting, update after mounting. Late-load cannot recreate the original snapshot.
Changing or removing applied rules needs a reboot. Third-party rules are never cleared.
Unavailable without writable proc controls (including expose_proc=0).
Independent FolkSU configuration. Does not install SUSFS or modify ksu_susfs / third-party settings.
Not supported by the detected capability set
Choose whether FolkSU controls this setting. Unmanaged does not reset the active kernel value.
Configuration cannot be read · import a valid file to recover
No kernel operation was performed. Apply explicitly or enable boot application.
Check the configuration and root authorization. After a timeout, refresh before retrying; an in-flight operation may still finish.
Acknowledged operations this boot, not proof of hiding effectiveness. After LKM reload, reboot before relying on replay state.
This session’s last apply request. Not a live inventory of all kernel rules.
Boot application is ON in this file.
Boot application is OFF in this file.
Replaces only FolkSU’s saved configuration after strict daemon validation. Does not apply now or clear active / third-party rules. If boot application is on, it may run on the next normal boot.
Saves default for both fields. Apply now to restore; merely removing a saved value does not restore the kernel.
Use default to keep each real kernel field. Both fields are required. These are saved targets, not live kernel readings.
Each field must be nonempty, under 65 UTF-8 bytes, and contain no control characters.
Saved replacement only. No live value is read here; removing the configuration does not restore an active spoof.
Enter nonempty text under 8192 UTF-8 bytes, without control characters.
Hide a target path through SUSFS. This is not a recursive directory rule.
Hide the target file’s memory mapping entries, such as in /proc/pid/maps. Does not hide directory entries.
Redirect the source file to a destination for a selected UID scope.
Use an absolute path under 256 UTF-8 bytes; no root-only path, whitespace, control characters, //, or . / .. segments.
Retry path resolution when the target is not yet available. Does not recursively hide children.
Use the full pre-mount metadata snapshot, including file size and link count.
Unsupported saved UID scope · select 0–2 to edit
Only verified scopes 0–2 are offered. Kernel acknowledgement does not prove the redirect affects every process in the scope.
Only available with the SUSFS LKM capability
GKI or KernelSU LKM mode alone does not identify SUSFS LKM.
A module name: 1–63 ASCII letters, digits or underscores. Does not load or unload modules.
Hide a mount prefix via exposed LKM controls. No global clearing of existing rules.
